context.focus: Battle module configuration, redis state keys, time-to-live (TTL) timers, architectural principles, background job definitions, and WebSocket event payload specifications.

principles_and_notes: Always use TTL's in redis so that user don't get stuck into any state forever if something occurs wrong.
Every function/job/step will update redis before it handover to another step.
Always use redis lock when any task or battle processing to avoid concurrency or race condition problems.
In all tasks if battle_state or other data not found fail silently. This fault tolerant behaviour strip concurrency edge cases mostly.
We will manage Constants and Registry of business constraints. Such as subject_code-subject_name map, each class's valid subjects, each subject's chapters names with numbers and so on.
Use MongoDB Upsert and BulkWrite as much as possible and efficiently to reduce database throughput. And use locks on MongoDB so that multiple workers cant create rat race condition.
While deleting/performing any task or job, delete all of its cache keys from redis to prevent stale data/state. And also save jobid before schedule, so that job can be traced later if needed.
To emit events from job of independent workers, use pub/sub. And before emitting any event check if battle room exist or not.

context.focus: WebSocket disconnect handling, live player answer submission during battle rounds, and voluntary battle forfeiture (QUIT_BATTLE) logic.

principles_and_notes: If a disconnected user is the last player in the room, the match immediately aborts and schedules finalize_battle without delay.
If other players remain in the room upon disconnect, a delayed forfeit job (FORFEIT_BATTLE_DELAY) is scheduled while notifying remaining players via USER_DISCONNECTED.
When both players submit their answers (players_answered == 2), the system schedules next_question after ROUND_TURN_DELAY.
